title: Fix input schema mutation in update_user
description:
MEDIUM: Pydantic model is mutated in endpoint (data.password = None).

Current state (users.py:78-80):
- Password is set to None after update
- Pydantic models should be treated as immutable

Fix:
- Use model_dump(exclude={'password'}) instead of mutation
- Pass explicit fields to service.update()

Files: app/api/v1/users.py

title: Add ownership check to GET /users/{id}
description:
MEDIUM: Any authenticated user can view any other user's profile (IDOR).

Current state (users.py:38-51):
- No ownership check on get_user endpoint
- Only requires authentication

Fix:
- Add check: current_user.id == user_id or current_user.is_superuser
- Return 404 for unauthorized access (don't reveal user exists)

Files: app/api/v1/users.py

title: Remove default SECRET_KEY
description:
MEDIUM: Default SECRET_KEY in source code risks insecure deployments.

Current state (config.py:29):
- SECRET_KEY has default value 'change-me-in-production'

Fix:
1. Remove default value (fail fast if not set)
2. Add validator to reject weak/default keys
3. Require minimum 32 characters

Files: app/core/config.py
close_reason: Removed default SECRET_KEY, added 32-char minimum validator

title: Fix authentication timing attack
description:
HIGH: Early return on missing user enables email enumeration via timing analysis.

Current state (user_service.py:33-40):
- Missing user returns immediately (fast)
- Wrong password runs bcrypt verification (slow)
- Attackers can measure response times to determine if email exists

Fix:
- Always run bcrypt verification even for missing users
- Use dummy hash for non-existent users to normalize timing

Files: app/services/user_service.py
close_reason: Fixed timing attack by running bcrypt on dummy hash for missing users

title: Fix rate limiter registration
description:
CRITICAL: Rate limiter is instantiated but never attached to app state, making all @limiter.limit() decorators non-functional.

Current state:
- auth.py:18 creates local Limiter instance
- main.py never registers it with app.state

Fix:
1. Create shared limiter in app/core/limiter.py
2. Register with app.state.limiter in main.py
3. Import shared limiter in auth.py

Files: app/main.py, app/api/v1/auth.py, app/core/limiter.py (new)
close_reason: Created shared limiter in app/core/limiter.py, registered with app.state

title: Implement token revocation with Redis
description:
HIGH: JWTs cannot be invalidated. Compromised refresh tokens remain valid for 7 days.

Requirements:
1. Add JTI (JWT ID) claim to tokens
2. Store refresh token JTIs in Redis with TTL
3. Check JTI validity on token refresh
4. Invalidate all user tokens on password change
5. Add logout endpoint to revoke current refresh token

Dependencies:
- Redis already in requirements.txt

Files: app/core/security.py, app/api/v1/auth.py, app/core/redis.py (new)
close_reason: Implemented Redis-based token revocation with JTI claims, logout endpoint, and password change invalidation

title: Strengthen password policy
description:
MEDIUM: Password policy only requires 8 characters, no complexity.

Current state (schemas/auth.py:33-35, schemas/user.py:13-17):
- Only length >= 8 check
- Duplicated validation in two files

Fix:
1. Increase minimum to 12 characters
2. Require uppercase, lowercase, and digit
3. Extract to shared validator function
4. Apply to both RegisterRequest and UserCreate/UserUpdate

Files: app/schemas/auth.py, app/schemas/user.py, app/core/validators.py (new)
close_reason: Created shared validator with 12-char min, uppercase, lowercase, digit requirements
